wa_martha_lake_airport_park_boulder_lynn.blurb: A single large glacial boulder sitting in a suburban county park in Lynnwood, in the northeast corner just beyond the skate park. The 14 problems are spread around its west, north, south and east faces, and a few of the lines are done on top rope. Difficulty runs from V1 to V5, with most of the problems landing between V1 and V3, so it suits beginners and anyone wanting a quick after-work session. The boulder is modest in size, the area around it is flat park ground, and parking is easy. Expect other park users nearby.

wa_bathtub_dome.blurb: A tiered crag on the hillside above Icicle Creek near Leavenworth. The walk in is steep and takes about three quarters of an hour, and that effort tends to keep the crowds away. Most of the 14 routes are traditional lines, with a handful of bolted ones mixed in, and they run from 5.6 up to the low 5.10s, with the bulk in the 5.9 range. It is a good pick for climbers who want quality moderate pitches and some quiet, and who do not mind a hard hike to reach the base.

wa_hag_crag.blurb: A small crag in the Lookout Point zone above the town of Index, just right of the Private Idaho wall. It has 14 routes, mostly trad with a few bolted lines, a top rope and one aid climb. Grades are mainly 5.6 to 5.7 and 5.9 to 5.11, so there is something for newer leaders as well as harder slab and crack climbing. The low-angle cracks make it a popular beginner stop, while the slabs see fewer visitors. Big-leaf maples shade the base for most of the day, which feels good in summer but means the rock is slow to dry after rain.

wi_1_the_instrumentals.blurb: A bouldering zone at the foot of a cliff band on Devil's Lake's West Bluff, the first of the upper-access areas you meet when hiking up the West Bluff Trail from the north end. It holds 14 problems on quartzite, from easy V1 slabs through the V2 to V4 middle ground to a few much harder lines in the V6 to V7 range. The area has a small number of standout problems and good views over the lake. It is a short hike up from the lot, so it works well for a quick session.

wi_hammer_wall_the_keyhole.blurb: A cluster of climbs on the lower level of Major Mass at Devil's Lake, between Major and Minor Mass. The Hammer Wall is a large, clean, east-facing face, and the Keyhole is a smaller cousin of the Doorway that marks the eastern edge. The 14 climbs are all trad or top rope on quartzite, with plenty of 5.4 to 5.7 routes and a few hard 5.11 and 5.12 outliers. Some lines can be done in as many as three pitches, but many parties link them in one or climb part way and scramble off west. The wall faces east, so it gets morning light.

wi_ghost_of_the_forest.blurb: A quartzite boulder zone low in the East Bluff North talus at Devil's Lake, down in the woods below the last parking lot. It holds 14 problems, all bouldering, with a wide spread: a few easy problems around V0 to V2, a solid block of V4s, and several hard lines up to V7. The terrain is a forested boulder field rather than an open crag, so it feels secluded and shady. It is a good stop for climbers who want to project in the V4 to V7 range among the trees.
